skill.name: parallel-task-spark
skill.description: Coordinates parallel execution of markdown plan tasks with Sparky subagents, dependency waves, TDD verification, local commits, and plan updates.
skill.summary: Run structured development plans through dependency-aware Sparky subagents with verification and local commit tracking.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: The static backtick findings are false positives from Markdown inline code and fenced templates, not Ruby or shell execution. I found no prompt injection text or data exfiltration intent. The main residual risk is execution of validation commands from user-provided plan content.

remediation.issue: Validation commands may come from untrusted plan content.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running commands copied from a plan, and prefer known project test commands.

remediation.issue: Parallel subagents can modify files and create local commits.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should start from a clean workspace and review task commits before merging.

semantic_findings.title: User-Provided Validation Commands
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to run exact validation commands or concrete validation steps from a plan. A malicious or untrusted plan could request destructive local commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly mention exact commands and running validation. The risk depends on plan trust, so this is a workflow risk rather than clear malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Large implementation plans are hard to coordinate when tasks can run in parallel. This skill schedules dependency waves, delegates to Sparky subagents, and records verified results.
actual_capabilities: Parses markdown plan files for task IDs, dependencies, descriptions, acceptance criteria, and validation notes.
Filters requested task subsets while preserving required dependencies.
Launches unblocked tasks in parallel with the Sparky agent role.
Requires TDD RED phase evidence or documented non-testable validation.
Checks subagent outputs, local commits, and plan log updates before moving to later waves.
Repeats dependency waves until the selected plan work is complete or blocked.
limitations: It requires a clear markdown plan with task IDs, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and validation notes.
It depends on available Sparky and test-writer subagents.
It can run validation commands from plans, so untrusted plans need review first.
It does not replace human code review before merging.

use_cases.title: Implement Large Plans
use_cases.description: Split a planned feature into parallel dependency waves while keeping verification and commits explicit.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Multi-Agent Work
use_cases.description: Assign independent tasks to Sparky subagents and keep each wave tied to dependency status.

use_cases.title: Preserve Test Evidence
use_cases.description: Require RED to GREEN evidence or documented alternative checks before marking tasks complete.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner use with one plan file.
prompt_templates.prompt:
/parallel-task-spark ./plans/auth-plan.md
Run every task in dependency order. Use RED to GREEN evidence where possible.

prompt_templates.title: Run Selected Tasks
prompt_templates.scenario: Execute only part of a plan.
prompt_templates.prompt:
/parallel-task-spark ./plans/profile-plan.md T1 T3 T7
Include any required dependencies before launching the selected tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Strict Validation
prompt_templates.prompt:
/parallel-task-spark ./plans/billing-plan.md
For each task, capture test evidence, changed files, commit status, and any deferred validation.

prompt_templates.title: Resume After Blockers
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced recovery after a failed wave.
prompt_templates.prompt:
/parallel-task-spark ./plans/migration-plan.md --tasks T4 T5 T6
Resume only unblocked tasks. Escalate failed tasks with blockers and exact missing evidence.

output_examples.input: A plan has T1 and T2 with no dependencies, and T3 depends on both.
output_examples.output: The skill launches T1 and T2 first. After both are verified and committed, it launches T3 and updates the plan log.

output_examples.input: A selected task depends on a setup task that was not requested.
output_examples.output: The skill includes the setup task, runs the selected task after the dependency completes, and reports verification evidence.

output_examples.input: A task cannot produce a useful failing test before implementation.
output_examples.output: The skill records why the task is not testable, defines alternative validation, and requires evidence before completion.

best_practices: Use clear task IDs, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and validation commands in the plan.
Run the skill only on trusted plans in repositories prepared for local commits.
Review generated commits and plan updates before merging work.
anti_patterns: Do not run it on ambiguous or untrusted plan files with unsafe validation commands.
Do not use it when parallel tasks edit the same files without coordination.
Do not treat its validation summary as a replacement for code review.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It reads a markdown plan, finds task dependencies, and launches Sparky subagents in dependency waves.

faq.question: Can I run only selected tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide task IDs, and the skill includes required dependencies when it builds the execution set.

faq.question: Does it write code itself?
faq.answer: It coordinates subagents that implement tasks. It also checks outputs, validation evidence, commits, and plan updates.

faq.question: Does it push changes?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs agents to commit locally and never push.

faq.question: What plan format works best?
faq.answer: Use headings for task IDs, a depends_on list, acceptance criteria, and clear validation steps.

faq.question: Can it handle failed tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews failures, retries when appropriate, or escalates blockers with a summary.
